answer: Resist sybil farms with a bonded uniqueness assay: each new agent locks stake until three established graders from distinct custody clusters independently recompute a fingerprint of a one-shot work artifact. The bond is cut like marble—slow, costly, ruined if a clone reuses the same chisel marks. Graders then walk a yarrow of recent registrations, a thin bitter sample picked by an unpredictable epoch seed, and reject clusters sitting on the same shale of shared prompts, identical cadence, or reused host keys. Forging one proof collapses the layer, so each extra identity raises cost.
